questions: What is the chemical formula for water?
A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
What force pulls objects toward the centre of the Earth?
Gravity attracts masses toward one another, pulling objects toward Earth's centre.
Which part of a plant mainly carries out photosynthesis?
Leaves contain chloroplasts packed with chlorophyll, where most photosynthesis happens.
What gas do plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
Plants take in carbon dioxide and, using light energy, convert it into sugars.
What is the centre of an atom called?
The nucleus holds the protons and neutrons at the core of an atom.
What state of matter is steam?
Steam is water in its gaseous state.
Which organ do humans use to breathe?
The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air and the blood.
What do we call animals that eat only plants?
Herbivores are adapted to eat plant material.
What is the closest star to Earth?
The Sun is a star about 150 million km away; Proxima Centauri is the next nearest.
What is the main gas in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume.
What is the body's largest organ?
The skin is the largest organ of the human body by surface area and weight.
What type of energy does a moving object have?
Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion.
Which blood cells help fight infection?
White blood cells (leukocytes) are part of the immune system.
What do magnets attract most strongly among these?
Iron is ferromagnetic and strongly attracted to magnets; aluminium and copper are not.
What is H in the periodic table?
H is the symbol for hydrogen, element number 1.
Which sense organ is used for hearing?
The ear converts sound waves into nerve signals.
What is the process of a liquid turning into a gas called?
Evaporation turns liquid into vapour; condensation is the reverse.
How many chambers does the human heart have?
The heart has two atria and two ventricles.
What is the atomic number of carbon?
Carbon has six protons; its most common isotope has a mass number of 12.
Which scientist proposed the theory of general relativity?
What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7 at 25 °C.
Which particle carries a negative electric charge?
Electrons carry a negative charge; protons are positive and neutrons are neutral.
What is the powerhouse of the cell that produces most of its ATP?
Mitochondria generate most of a cell's ATP through cellular respiration.
What is the speed of light in a vacuum, approximately?
Light travels at 299,792 km/s in a vacuum.
Which gas makes up most of the Sun's mass?
The Sun is roughly three-quarters hydrogen by mass, with most of the rest helium.
What molecule carries genetic information in most living organisms?
What is the chemical symbol for gold?
Au comes from the Latin word for gold, aurum.
What is the SI unit of force?
Force is measured in newtons; one newton accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s².
Scurvy results from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
What type of bond involves the sharing of electron pairs between atoms?
In a covalent bond, atoms share pairs of electrons.
What is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust?
Oxygen makes up about 46% of the crust by mass, mostly bound in silicate minerals.
Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red cells?
O-negative red cells lack A, B and RhD antigens, so most recipients can receive them.
What do you call a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed?
A catalyst lowers the activation energy and is not used up in the reaction.
Which part of the human eye controls how much light enters?
The iris adjusts the size of the pupil to regulate incoming light.
Which scientist is famous for the laws of motion and universal gravitation?
Newton set out his laws of motion and gravitation in the Principia (1687).
What is the name for animals that are active mainly at night?
Nocturnal animals are active at night and rest during the day.
What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
Na comes from the Latin natrium.
Seismographs record ground motion caused by earthquakes.
Which noble gas is commonly used in bright advertising signs that glow red-orange?
Neon gives off a characteristic red-orange glow in discharge tubes.
What is the study of fungi called?
Mycology is the branch of biology concerned with fungi.
Which planet's moon Titan has a thick nitrogen atmosphere?
Titan, Saturn's largest moon, has a dense nitrogen-rich atmosphere.
What is the name of the constant approximately equal to 6.022 × 10²³ per mole?
The Avogadro constant is the number of particles in one mole of a substance.
Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
Fluorine has a Pauling electronegativity of about 3.98, the highest of any element.
In genetics, what is the term for different versions of the same gene?
Alleles are variant forms of a gene at the same locus.
What is the half-life of carbon-14, to the nearest thousand years?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years, which makes radiocarbon dating possible.
Which subatomic particle was discovered by James Chadwick in 1932?
Chadwick's discovery of the neutron earned him the 1935 Nobel Prize in Physics.
What is the most abundant protein in the human body?
Collagen is the main structural protein in connective tissue.
Which law states that the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume at constant temperature?
Boyle's law: P × V is constant for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature.
What is the only metal that is a liquid at room temperature?
Mercury is the only metal liquid at standard room temperature; bromine is a liquid non-metal.
Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis in a cell?
Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into proteins.
What is the name of the effect where light shining on a metal ejects electrons?
Einstein's explanation of the photoelectric effect won him the 1921 Nobel Prize.
Which human gland is often called the 'master gland'?
The pituitary gland regulates many other endocrine glands.
What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
Absolute zero is 0 K, which equals -273.15 °C (or -459.67 °F).
Which scientist first isolated penicillin's antibacterial effect from mould in 1928?
Fleming noticed that Penicillium mould killed bacteria in 1928.
What is the name of the boundary between Earth's crust and mantle?
The 'Moho' marks the change from crust to mantle.
What type of rock is formed from cooled magma or lava?
Igneous rocks form when molten rock solidifies.
Which element is the main component of steel besides iron?
Steel is an alloy of iron with a small amount of carbon.
In which part of the human body would you find the cochlea?
The cochlea is the spiral-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear.
Which branch of physics studies the behaviour of matter at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles?
Quantum mechanics describes nature at the smallest scales.
What is the chemical symbol for tungsten?
W comes from wolfram, tungsten's alternative name.
Which process do cells use to divide into two genetically identical daughter cells?
Mitosis produces two identical daughter nuclei; meiosis produces sex cells.
What is the hardest substance in the human body?
Enamel, the outer layer of teeth, is the hardest substance in the human body.
Which scale measures the hardness of minerals from 1 to 10?
Friedrich Mohs devised the scale in 1812; talc is 1 and diamond is 10.
